extraction.name: TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating language agents on real-world travel planning with multiple constraints, tool use, and planning over a closed sandbox environment.
extraction.creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was constructed by creating a static and closed sandbox environment, sourcing original data from publicly available internet data and Kaggle datasets, modifying the data by adding, deleting, and altering keys and values, and manually annotating 1,225 travel queries with reference plans. The authors also performed detailed review and quality control of every query and plan.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Publicly available internet data; Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset; Google Distance Matrix API; Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset; Google Places API; Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: FlightSearch data extracted from 2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01; the benchmark queries and plans use dates in 2022.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Original data were modified by adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values to suit the benchmark requirements. For FlightSearch, price was generated by multiplying distance by a random factor ranging from 0.2 to 0.5. For DistanceMatrix, price was computed from distance using factors of 1 for self-driving and 0.15 for taxi. Restaurants and accommodations were randomly assigned to cities, and restaurants were randomly categorized by cuisine; accommodations were assigned room rules.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For FlightSearch, only selected fields such as FlightDate, DepTime, ArrTime, ActualElapsedTime, Distance, OriginCityName, and DestCityName were retained while other values were discarded. For RestaurantSearch, Restaurant Name and Average Cost were extracted. For AttractionSearch, essential fields such as Name, Address, Phone, Website, Latitude, and Longitude were retained. For AccommodationSearch, key details such as NAME, room type, price, minimum nights, review rate number, and maximum occupancy were extracted.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 20 graduate students meticulously annotated reference plans for synthesized queries. A plan was considered eligible only if it met all constraints in the evaluation script. The authors then reviewed every query and plan and corrected errors. Budgets were recalibrated using costs from the human-annotated plans.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: One plan was deemed eligible only if it satisfied all constraints in the evaluation script. The paper reports that 1,225 validated query-plan pairs were created through human verification and quality control.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate natural language queries; GPT-4-Turbo was used for key components extraction in experiments; ReAct and Reflexion were used as planning strategies in evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state they will release their evaluation scripts. They also prohibit cheating in the validation and test sets to preserve fairness and reliability. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is provided.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes user needs and constraints such as budget, room type, room rules, cuisine preferences, transportation preferences, number of people, travel dates, and city/state locations. It also includes accommodation-related attributes such as pet-friendliness, children under 10, no smoking, no parties, and no visitors.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper positions the benchmark as a tool for advancing language agents toward more capable real-world planning. It notes that commonsense definitions may vary and encourages broader discussion to improve evaluation. The benchmark is intended to support future research and development of more capable agents.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note that using a static sandbox avoids variability and potential biases introduced by dynamic data. They also state that commonsense evaluation criteria are based on author consensus, implying possible subjectivity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited to a static and closed sandbox environment and may not capture dynamic real-world changes. The paper notes that current evaluation criteria for commonsense are based on author consensus. The benchmark is challenging for current agents, and the paper emphasizes that existing agents struggle with multi-constraint planning and tool use.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and test benchmarking for evaluating language agents on tool use and complex travel planning; also used for sole-planning and two-stage evaluation settings.
